newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan buys 26,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat at tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buys 26,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat at tender.

text.p: The Taiwan Flour Mills Association bought a shipment of 26,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat at a tender on Thursday, traders said.

A March 20 government ban on pork exports sparked by an outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease has slashed the island's demand for imports of feed corn and soybeans, but the impact on Taiwan's wheat demand has been limited, traders said.
"Feed is only a small part of wheat imports," a buyer said.
Freight for the shipment was fixed at 24.00 per tonne, traders said.
The shipment, sourced from three suppliers, contains Dark Northern Spring (DNS), Hard Red Winter (HRW) and White Wheat (WW) and is slated for delivery from the Pacific Northwest, traders said.
